skills.does: Work out the review dates for spaced repetition from a starting date.
examples: spaced repetition schedule doubling each time
review dates one week and one month out

skills.does: Split a list into consecutive groups of a fixed size — deal items into groups of four.
Count how many times each item appears in a list, ranked most common first.
examples: count how many of each are in this list

skills.does: Remove repeated items from a list, keeping the first of each and the original order.
examples: remove the duplicates from this list

skills.does: Find what is in one list but not the other, in both directions.
examples: what is in the first list but not the second
compare these two lists of numbers
are these two lists the same

skills.does: Flatten a list of nested lists into a single flat list.
Keep only the items appearing on both lists.
examples: what is in both of these lists
do these two lists overlap at all

skills.does: Draw people into random pairs or teams from a seed.
examples: pair these four people up, seed 7
draw pairs from five names, seed 1
split six into teams of three, seed 42

skills.does: Pick one or more items at random from a list, from a seed so the pick can be repeated.
examples: pick one of these at random with seed 7
choose a name from the list, seed 1

skills.does: Count from one number to another in steps, listing every number on the way.
Jumble any list into a random order from a seed.
examples: shuffle the running order with seed 42

skills.does: Put a list of items in order — alphabetically, numerically, or in natural order where numbers inside names count.
examples: sort file names in natural order

skills.does: Merge two lists into one, dropping repeats.
Combine two or more lists position by position — pair each name with its score.
examples: combine names and ages into records

skills.does: Split an amount across shares in proportion to their weights.
examples: share 100 out in equal parts between three
divide 100 in a one to two ratio

skills.does: Work out an arithmetic expression exactly. Reads % as a percentage.
examples: what is 2 to the power of 10

skills.does: Work out a factorial — multiply every whole number from 1 up to n together.
Give the nth Fibonacci number, or the first n of them.
Write an amount of money the way a currency is normally written, with its symbol and decimal places.
Write a number with thousands separators, a set number of decimals, or in compact form like 1.2k.
Reduce a fraction like 6/8 to its lowest terms.
Find the biggest number that divides them all exactly.
Say whether a whole number is prime, and give a divisor if it is not.
Find the smallest number they all go into.
examples: when do buses every 12 and 18 minutes coincide

skills.does: Read a number written any human way — "1.2k", "$3,400", "three quarters of a million" — as a plain number.
examples: what is twenty five as a number

skills.does: Split a set of numbers into percentage shares of their total.
examples: what percentage of the total is each of 30 50 20

skills.does: Percentage change between two numbers, and the difference in plain terms.
examples: my rent went from 1200 to 1350, what percent increase is that

skills.does: Take a percentage of a number — 15% of 240, or 20 percent of a bill.
Break a whole number down into the prime numbers it is made of.
examples: what are the prime factors of 97

skills.does: Multiply a list of numbers you give together.
Solve a proportion when one of the four terms is missing.
examples: solve this proportion, 3 is to 4 as 9 is to what

skills.does: Round a number to a number of decimal places or significant figures.
examples: round 1234.5678 to the nearest whole number

skills.does: Solve a quadratic equation — the roots of ax² + bx + c = 0, real or complex.
Split an amount into equal parts, assigning the leftover pennies so the parts add back up.
Add a list of numbers up to one final total.
examples: what is the total of my expenses 12.50 8.20 45
sum these negative and positive numbers

skills.does: Add the ordinal suffix to a number — 3 becomes 3rd, 42 becomes 42nd.
Work out what share one number is of another, as a percentage — what proportion 18 is of 24, or a score out of a maximum.
examples: i got 47 out of 60, what percent is that

skills.does: Divide an income into budget categories by percentage, using 50/30/20 or ratios you set.
Find the hours when everyone is inside their working day, across time zones.
examples: when can London and New York meet
common working hours for London and Berlin
can London and Tokyo find a meeting time
